problem_solved: Skills are created and changed without knowing whether they actually improve performance
how_it_works: Interview about intent; write SKILL.md; 2-3 test cases in evals/evals.json; run each with and without the skill; grade via subagent or script; benchmark pass rate, time, and tokens; feedback viewer; description optimization with a 60/40 train/test split
inputs: Skill intent; test scenarios; user feedback
runtime_overhead: unknown (each test runs twice: with and without)
evidence: Documentation only; no public measurements found
license: LICENSE.txt in folder — license type not read (G-005)
limitations: Few test cases by default; some features need subagents or a browser
potential_value: Ready implementation of baseline-vs-skill comparison — directly relevant to the evaluation framework and to developing every harness skill

problem_solved: Checking frontend behavior, debugging UI, capturing screenshots and browser logs
how_it_works: Python Playwright scripts (headless Chromium); scripts/with_server.py manages starting and stopping local servers; reconnaissance: wait for networkidle, screenshot or inspect DOM, then act on selectors
license: LICENSE.txt in folder — license type not read (G-005)
limitations: Python only; no dependency manifest or versions
potential_value: Basis for agent-driven UI verification before completing a task

problem_solved: Building MCP servers whose tools are genuinely useful to an LLM
how_it_works: 4 phases: research and planning (tool design principles, naming, context management, error messages); implementation (Python FastMCP or TypeScript SDK); review and test with MCP Inspector; create 10 read-only verifiable evaluation questions
dependencies: Python FastMCP or TypeScript MCP SDK (v2 recommended)
license: LICENSE.txt in folder — license type not read (G-005)
potential_value: Relevant only if the harness needs its own MCP server; contains tool design principles for agents

problem_solved: Users act on answers without checking facts, assumptions, or missing context
how_it_works: After a substantive answer the user may act on: 2-3 optional follow-up questions pointing to specific parts of the answer; at most once per conversation; not triggered for code the user will run
license: LICENSE.txt in folder — license type not read (G-005)
limitations: Explicitly excluded for code the user will run — low relevance to software engineering
potential_value: Inspiration for review points on decisions and plans (domain H)

problem_solved: Skills that document imagined problems instead of real ones
how_it_works: 5 steps: identify gaps by running without the skill; build 3 evaluation scenarios; measure a baseline; write minimal instructions; iterate and compare against the baseline. Also: Claude A writes the skill and Claude B tests it in real use
dependencies: None (the docs state there is no built-in way to run the evaluations)
limitations: No built-in runner — needs an implementation (C-001 is one)
potential_value: Core principle for every harness component: prove improvement over the baseline before adoption
notes: Docs also recommend testing with Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus

problem_solved: Coding agents skip design, planning, tests, and verification
how_it_works: Plugin with skills, a SessionStart hook, scripts, and tests. Prescribed flow: brainstorming -> git worktree -> writing-plans -> subagent-driven-development or executing-plans (with TDD) -> code review between tasks -> finishing-a-development-branch. Skills are presented as 'Mandatory workflows, not suggestions'
token_overhead: High fixed cost: bootstrap skill injected every session (C-007, C-008) plus all skill descriptions; not measured
runtime_overhead: High: subagent per task plus reviews (by design)
evidence: No quantitative evidence on the page; anecdotes; mentions a 'drill' eval harness in superpowers-evals (repo not reachable, G-010)
limitations: Heavy and opinionated; mandatory skill checks before every response; supports many harnesses
potential_value: Source of several strong individual skills; whole-framework adoption conflicts with the minimal-harness principle
notes: Also ships per-harness plugin folders (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, others)

problem_solved: Agent forgets to use available skills
how_it_works: Requires invoking a skill before ANY response, including clarifying questions: 'If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply ... you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.' Red-flag table against skipping. User instructions rank above skills
token_overhead: ~450-500 words injected every session (estimate from page length)
runtime_overhead: Extra skill-tool calls on every task (not measured)
limitations: Very low trigger threshold may cause unnecessary skill loads and tokens on simple tasks
potential_value: Inspiration only: shows the cost of forcing skill usage; the harness should measure trigger accuracy instead

problem_solved: Bootstrap instructions must be present in every session
how_it_works: SessionStart hook reads skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md, wraps it in <EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT> tags, and returns it as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext for Claude Code (other formats for Cursor, Copilot CLI). Always exits 0; avoids external commands so it works with a broken PATH
potential_value: Reusable pattern for injecting a small, always-needed context file at session start

problem_solved: Building the wrong thing because intent and the 'why' were never clarified
how_it_works: Assess what the request already answers; one question at a time; play back understanding in 200-300 word chunks; propose 2-3 approaches with a recommendation; write design doc to docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md; subagent 'builder check' for gaps; hard gate: 'Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc'; hand off to writing-plans
limitations: Long skill; may slow small tasks (it exempts quick fully specified requests)
potential_value: Strong fit for the 'user only decides and reviews' goal: explicit approval gate on a written design

subcategory: Implementation plans for a fresh implementer
problem_solved: Implementers (human or agent) guess decisions the spec did not make
how_it_works: Plan = 'the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone'. Per task: exact file paths, interfaces with signatures, test code with spec values, expected failing/passing output, commit. Header includes Global Constraints and Review Focus (5 likely real-world failures, each with a test). Self-review checklist incl. proportion (plan not several times longer than spec). Saved to docs/superpowers/plans/. User chooses subagent-driven or native execution
potential_value: Plan format directly reusable for agent handoffs (domain A, H)

subcategory: Plan execution with a subagent per task
problem_solved: Long tasks degrade a single context; self-review misses defects
how_it_works: Fresh implementer subagent per task (writes full report to a file, returns short status); task reviewer gives two verdicts: spec compliance and quality; capped fix loop with model escalation; ledger file tracks progress because memory does not survive compaction; briefs and diffs passed as files; review diff from recorded BASE commit (not HEAD~1); no parallel implementers; explicit model tier per dispatch; stop only for irreversible, security-sensitive, external side effect (merge/push/publish), or broken plan
dependencies: Subagents; git; helper scripts (sdd-workspace, task-brief, review-package)
token_overhead: High (fresh context per task and review); docs say higher than inline execution
limitations: Costly; requires mostly independent tasks; long skill (~2,500 words)
potential_value: Most detailed handoff and context-passing practice found so far; ledger and stop-conditions map directly to the agent-managed goal

problem_solved: Agents write code first and tests later, or tests that never failed
how_it_works: Iron Law: 'NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST'; code written before its test must be deleted; watch each test fail for the expected reason; full suite must pass with pristine output; 11-row rationalization table and 13 red flags
evidence: Practice (TDD) is established; no evidence for this skill's effect
limitations: Very rigid ('delete and start over'); exceptions need human approval
potential_value: Strong discipline enforcement; compare with C-017 in evaluation

problem_solved: Symptom fixes and guess-and-check debugging
how_it_works: Four phases: root cause investigation, pattern analysis (compare with working code), single hypothesis tested minimally, implementation with failing test first. Iron Law: 'NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST'. After 3 failed fixes: stop and question the architecture
potential_value: The 3-fix limit is a concrete escalation rule

problem_solved: Agents claim success without running checks
how_it_works: Iron Law: 'NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE'. Gate: identify the proving command, run it fresh, read full output and exit code, compare with claim, then state result with evidence. Evidence table: tests, linter, build, bug fixed, regression test red-green, VCS diff for agent work, line-by-line requirements checklist
limitations: Instruction only — not enforced (see batch 1: hooks enforce, instructions request)
potential_value: High value and low cost; candidate to pair with a Stop hook for enforcement

problem_solved: Skills that do not change agent behavior
how_it_works: RED: run a pressure scenario with a subagent without the skill and record rationalizations; GREEN: minimal skill addressing them; REFACTOR: close new loopholes. 'NO SKILL WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST'. Testing differs by skill type (discipline, technique, pattern, reference). Description says only when to use, never summarizes the workflow
potential_value: Independent confirmation of the baseline-first method in C-005; adds pressure-scenario testing

problem_solved: Agent-assisted work drifting into 'vibe coding' without alignment, shared language, or feedback loops
how_it_works: ~29 skills in engineering/ and productivity/, split into user-invoked and model-invoked. Themes: alignment via grilling, shared language via GLOSSARY.md (DDD), feedback loops (TDD, debugging), deep modules (Ousterhout, Beck). One-time /setup-matt-pocock-skills per repo
dependencies: Claude Code plugin system; issue tracker for some skills
token_overhead: Lower than C-006 by design: many skills are user-invoked only (not measured)
evidence: No quantitative evidence; based on cited books and author experience
limitations: Some skills depend on an issue tracker; criticizes GSD, BMAD, Spec Kit as removing control
potential_value: Closest match to the 'small, composable, minimal' principle

problem_solved: Tests coupled to implementation; tests written for imagined behavior
how_it_works: Agree public interface and test seams with the user first; one seam, one failing test, one minimal implementation per cycle (vertical slices, tracer bullets); refactoring moved to code review; anti-patterns: mocking internals, tautological expected values, horizontal slicing
evidence: Practice established; no evidence for this skill
limitations: Needs the user to agree seams (a human checkpoint)
potential_value: Lighter than C-012 and focused on test quality (tautological tests); compare in evaluation

problem_solved: Hard bugs and performance regressions debugged by guessing
how_it_works: Phases: 0 redact secrets; 1 build a fast deterministic agent-runnable loop that goes red on this bug ('Refuse to give up'); 2 reproduce and minimise; 3 3-5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses shown to the user; 4 instrument one variable at a time with tagged logs; 5 regression test then fix; 6 cleanup and record the correct hypothesis in the commit
potential_value: Adds secret redaction and multi-hypothesis ranking not in C-013

problem_solved: Shallow modules and pass-through layers that are hard to test and navigate
how_it_works: Shared vocabulary (module, interface, implementation, adapter, seam, depth, leverage, locality); deletion test; 'One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.'; DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md runs parallel subagents to design alternative interfaces
evidence: Based on Ousterhout and Feathers; no evidence for the skill
potential_value: Concrete, checkable design heuristics for architecture review (domain F)

problem_solved: Reviews that mix standards and spec, letting one mask the other
how_it_works: Three-dot diff against a fixed point; two parallel subagents with fresh context: Standards (repo docs plus 12 Fowler code smells as judgement calls) and Spec (missing requirements, scope creep); reports kept separate: 'Do not merge or rerank findings'; each report capped at 400 words
outputs: Two review sections and a one-line summary
limitations: Spec axis skipped when no spec exists
potential_value: Spec-compliance axis is something a generic review lacks

problem_solved: Ad-hoc implementation without tests or review
how_it_works: User-invoked only (disable-model-invocation). Steps: intake spec/ticket; TDD at agreed seams (C-017); typecheck and single tests regularly, full suite at end; code-review (C-020); commit
potential_value: Shows a minimal composition of TDD + review in ~200 words

problem_solved: Research floods the main context and relies on secondary sources
how_it_works: Background agent with fresh context; primary sources only; each claim cited; one Markdown file saved where the repo keeps notes
token_overhead: Low in main context (work done in background)
potential_value: Matches this project's own research rules; usable as-is for research tasks

problem_solved: The same agent mistakes repeat across sessions
how_it_works: Reviews a session (from logs if needed) across 7 areas incl. automated checks, coding standards, tool economy, no-ops in steering files; mechanical rules should become deterministic checks (lint, pre-commit, CI) rather than prose; proposes ranked improvements, does not edit
potential_value: Fits the goal of agents maintaining their own setup while the user approves changes

problem_solved: Context lost between sessions or agents
how_it_works: Compacts the conversation into a document with summary, suggested skills, and references (paths/URLs) to existing artifacts instead of copies; redacts secrets; saved to the OS temp directory
limitations: Saved to temp dir, not the repo — may be lost
potential_value: Reference-not-copy rule directly supports token efficiency (domain A)

problem_solved: Plans with unresolved or silently assumed decisions
how_it_works: Map the topic as a design tree; ask numbered rounds covering the frontier (questions whose prerequisites are settled), each with a recommended answer so 'yes' accepts it; facts are looked up by a subagent, decisions always go to the user; stops when the frontier is empty and nothing is assumed
potential_value: Batching decisions with recommended answers minimizes user effort — fits 'only decide and review'

problem_solved: Work larger than one session loses its decisions and direction
how_it_works: One map issue (wayfinder:map) with child decision tickets and native blocking links in the issue tracker; ticket types: research (AFK, subagent), prototype (HITL), grilling (HITL), task; one ticket resolved per session; resolved decisions summarized on the map; unknown areas kept as 'fog'
dependencies: Issue tracker (local markdown by default); C-025
potential_value: Persistent, reviewable decision state outside the context window — strong fit for domain H
